summary:
Read-only audit of the F-16A Block 15: flight model, simple-controls assist, HUD, camera and audio. The repo was not modified. Scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-spacex/49448258-b837-551e-9b35-7fac201f56d4/scratchpad/diag/ (h1–h4.mjs for headless flights, cam.mjs for in-browser camera measurements and HUD screenshots).

AUDIO: the F-16 has no sound at all. Grepping sound/audio/Audio in src/sim/f16*.js, src/ui/f16Hud.js and src/data/f16*.js finds nothing. There is no #f16-sound button, and KeyM is not in f16Fly's CODES (src/sim/f16Fly.js:105-106). Because f16Fly calls stopImmediatePropagation on every key (f16Fly.js:116), M currently does nothing during a flight. The GT3 and H2R both have the pattern this should copy: an AudioWorklet synth with oscillator fallback, opt-in on the M key, a #xxx-sound button with aria-pressed, suspend while the tab is hidden, and stop() on pause and end (gt3Sound.js:129-225, gt3Drive.js:206/236/260/535/562/594; h2rSound.js:119-203, h2rRide.js:48/73/85/291/330/340).

FLIGHT MODEL: tools/f16-check.mjs passes 28/28 in 1.5 s. The published-data path (Morelli fit, TP-1538 table VI thrust, the 1976 atmosphere, FCS limits) is sound. Measured: AB take-off rotates at 135 kt and lifts off at 174 kt after 415 m; roll rate 303°/s; the α limiter holds 25.6°; landing at 136 kt with 2.44 m/s sink; braking from 140 kt stops in 910 m (23 s). With full aft stick at idle it settles at α≈25° and 133 kt, sinking ~4,400 fpm, with no wing drop. A vertical climb at idle does not tail-slide: the FCS pulls it over at α≤20°.

I found three severe handling defects that the current tests miss:
1. Ground handling tips the jet over: any sustained steering input rolls it onto a wingtip, even at 5 kt.
2. In simple controls the throttle stays latched in full afterburner after the take-off, and the 8° climb is never levelled off. Hands-off, it reaches M1.65 at 43,000 ft in 4 min and 83,000 ft at 7 min.
3. Holding S on a gear-down approach ends in a crash at 25 m/s sink.

HUD and camera:
- The HUD never shows the runway cue, although f16Fly already computes readout.runway (f16Fly.js:510).
- In the cockpit view the pitch ladder covers the whole screen and runs over the control bar. It is not tied to the HUD combiner mesh, which sits below the drawn symbology.
- The chase camera lags behind in proportion to speed: 49 m behind at 80 m/s, 107 m at 350 m/s.
- In a vertical climb the chase camera looks straight up with up=(0,1,0) (measured camera direction y=0.996), which is a degenerate lookAt.

Smaller items: f16Assist.js:192 uses atmosphere(s.pos.y) instead of s.alt; FCS.departure (f16Aero.js:121) is dead data; the 20° flaperon droop is visual only.

findings.title: No F-16 audio exists; no HUD Sound button, M key swallowed
findings.evidence: grep -niE 'sound|audio' over src/sim/f16*.js src/ui/f16Hud.js src/data/f16*.js returns nothing. The f16Hud bar (src/ui/f16Hud.js:29-33) has Chase, Simple, Pause, Runway and End buttons only. The CODES set at src/sim/f16Fly.js:105-106 lacks KeyM, and f16Fly.js:116 calls stopImmediatePropagation on every key, so M does nothing in flight. main.js:666-673 passes no onSound. The guide's F-16 card (src/ui/hud.js:179-185) lists no M, while the GT3 and H2R cards do (hud.js:195, 205). For comparison, GT3 and H2R each have a full AudioWorklet engine.
findings.fix: Add src/sim/f16Sound.js on the gt3Sound/h2rSound pattern. Wire it into f16Fly (KeyM, setSound, update/stop) and add the #f16-sound button to f16Hud. Details are in the plan, section A.

findings.title: Ground handling: any sustained steering rolls the F-16 onto a wingtip (crash), even at 5 kt
findings.evidence:
diag/h2.mjs runs a flat runway with a constant pedal input. Every case crashes with what:'airframe'; bank reaches 27-29°, and the wheel loads read nose/left/right ≈ 5/76/0 kN:
- 5 kt, yaw 1: crash after 9.6 s, yaw rate 43°/s.
- 15 kt, yaw 0.5: crash.
- 30 kt, yaw 0.3: crash.
- 60 kt, yaw 0.3: crash.
- 100 kt, yaw 0.2: crash.

In simple controls (diag/h3.mjs), holding W and pressing D for 0.5 s at 80 kt crashes the airframe at 105 kt. A 0.2 s tap is fine.

Cause: steering is a geometric angle with only a mild speed schedule, clamp(32 - V*0.6, 5, 32)° (f16Flight.js:371). At 30 kt with 0.3 pedal that is 6.8° on a 4.0 m wheelbase, i.e. V²·tanδ/L ≈ 0.7 g asked of the tyres. The lateral tyre law at f16Flight.js:389 is a velocity damper capped at 0.7·Fn, so the tyres can deliver more than the static tip-over limit. That limit is about 0.54 g: CG height 1.845 m (CG.y), and the CG sits 0.997 m from the nose-to-main tip line given the 2.36 m track, 4.0 m wheelbase and CG 3.52 m aft of the nose wheel. The jet rolls over before the tyres slide. In simple mode the assist also sets yaw = roll on the ground (f16Assist.js:180-181), so A/D gives full nose-wheel steering at any speed.
findings.fix:
1. In f16Flight.js:371, limit the steering angle by lateral acceleration: δmax = min(32°, atan(0.3·g·GEAR.wheelbase / max(V,1)²)), marked ≈.
2. Replace the lateral law at f16Flight.js:389 with a slip-angle tyre: slip = atan2(vs, max(|vl|, 0.5)), Fs = −μy·Fn·tanh(slip/6°), with μy ≈ 0.55 on hard ground and 0.35 on soft (≈). Combine it with the longitudinal force by friction circle: if |(Fl,Fs)| > μ·Fn, scale both down.
3. In f16Assist.js ground branch (lines 180-181), turn A/D into a yaw-rate command, rCmd = turn·min(20°/s, 0.3g/V), and close the loop on s.w.z (body r) to set pilot.yaw. With no A/D input and rolling above 30 kt, hold the runway heading: yaw = k·(headingErr) + k2·(cross-track), using toRunway.

findings.title: Simple controls: throttle stays in full afterburner after take-off, the 8° climb is never levelled, and the jet rockets to 83,000 ft
findings.evidence:
diag/h1.mjs holds W for 25 s and then lets go:
- Lift-off at 155 kt; the gear comes up at 15 s.
- The throttle stays at 1.00 (power 100) for the rest of the flight.
- t=60 s: M1.10 at 6,074 ft. t=240 s: M1.65 at 43,394 ft. t=420 s: 82,839 ft, 89 KCAS, then it falls at γ −16° at about 100 KCAS.
- Fuel goes from 3,100 to 1,252 kg in 15 min.

Causes:
- f16Assist.js:171 only moves the throttle while W or S is held, so it latches.
- f16Assist.js:186 sets gammaCmd = max(8, γ) on the ground, and nothing ever levels the climb.
- The low-speed protection (f16Assist.js:230-233) sets throttle=1 and never gives it back.
- The approach autothrottle runs only if st.gearAuto (f16Assist.js:237). If the visitor raises the gear with G before the auto gear-up at 60 m AGL, gearAuto stays false and the approach is flown with whatever throttle is latched, often full AB.
findings.fix:
Add a speed-hold autothrottle to f16Assist:
- New fields st.vHold (KCAS) and st.touched.
- Airborne, W held: throttle rises as now, and st.vHold = current KCAS on release. S works the same, and also deploys the speed brakes.
- With neither held: a PI loop on vHold − kcas drives the throttle, capped at 0.77 (no AB) unless vHold exceeds what MIL can sustain. Clamp vHold to 200…600 KCAS.
- Initialise vHold = 350 KCAS at the auto gear-up.
- The low-speed protection becomes 'while slow': throttle = max(throttle, 1) only while kcas < 180, then back to the hold.
- Auto level-off: if ↑/↓ have not been touched since the take-off, ramp gammaCmd to 0 between 4,000 and 5,000 ft AGL.
- Set st.gearAuto = true whenever the gear goes up in the air, by G as well as automatically.
- Use atmosphere(s.alt) instead of s.pos.y (f16Assist.js:192).
- Publish st.vHold in the readout and draw 'A/T 350' in the HUD.

findings.title: Simple controls: holding S on a gear-down approach stalls into a 25 m/s gear-collapse crash; Auto-GCAS with the gear down is too late
findings.evidence:
diag/h4.mjs starts on a 3° path at 150 kt from 300 m, gear down, autothrottle on. Holding S for 30 s ends in CRASH gear at 25.3 m/s sink, 117 kt, min 92 KCAS. Holding it for 8 s recovers (min 109 KCAS).

Cause: with the gear down the GCAS triggers only on tti<2.5 s && sink>7 m/s (f16Assist.js:202), but the gear fails at about 5 m/s (f16Flight.js:368). Holding S puts the throttle at idle with the speed brakes out, while the path hold drives α to the 25° limiter.
findings.fix:
With the gear down:
- Floor the speed: while kcas < 135, throttle = max(throttle, PI to 135 kt), whatever S says; S only opens the speed brakes.
- Trigger GCAS on tti < 4 s && sink > 4 m/s.
- Cap gammaCmd so the predicted sink at AGL<30 m stays under 3 m/s.

findings.title: HUD has no runway cue although readout.runway is computed; visitors cannot find the runway to land
findings.evidence: f16Fly.js:510 publishes runway: { along, across, heading, name }. f16Hud.js never reads r.runway (grep 'runway' in f16Hud.js finds only the button's title). The simple-mode hint at f16Hud.js:34 says 'G gear: it holds 150 kt and flares for you', but nothing tells the visitor where runway 28 is.
findings.fix:
In f16Hud.update, below the heading:
- Draw 'RWY 28  x.x NM' with the bearing to the threshold, computed from r.position and the threshold point.
- Add a caret on the heading scale at the runway's bearing.
- Within 10 NM and aligned within 30°, add a glide-slope dot: the deviation from the 3° path is (alt − tan3°·dist).

Put the maths in an exported pure function runwayCue(r) so f16-check can test it headless.

findings.title: Cockpit HUD symbology is not tied to the combiner: the ladder fills the screen and overprints the control bar
findings.evidence: In diag/hud_cockpit.jpg the ladder labels run from 30 to 35 down over the .f16-bar keys at y≈610-670 px. f16Hud.js:116-150 draws ±85° wherever it projects. The combiner mesh 'f16-hud-combiner' (vehicles/f16.js:483) appears at roughly y 430-555 px, while the symbology is centred at H*0.46 (f16Hud.js:99).
findings.fix:
In cockpit view:
- Clip the drawing (g.save; g.beginPath; g.rect(...); g.clip()) to the screen rectangle of the combiner's four corners, projected from the mesh each frame, or to a fixed box of about ±12° around the boresight if the combiner is unreliable.
- Take cx and cy from the boresight projection of the airframe's +x axis from the eye, not from H*0.46.
- Skip ladder rungs whose projected y falls inside the bar's getBoundingClientRect.

findings.title: Chase camera: lag grows with speed (49 m at 80 m/s, 107 m at 350 m/s); degenerate lookAt in a vertical climb
findings.evidence:
diag/cam.mjs, real app, chase camera after 4 s of steady flight: distance to the CG 49.0 / 65.0 / 88.5 / 107.4 m at 80 / 150 / 250 / 350 m/s, against 26 m designed. The cause is f16Fly.js:291-292: chase.lerp(_cam, 1-exp(-4dt)) on the world position lags v/4 behind.

In a vertical climb the camera direction has y = 0.996 and camera.up stays (0,1,0) (f16Fly.js:296), which makes lookAt degenerate. The chase direction is clamped only for dives (_v.y ≥ −0.6, f16Fly.js:288).
findings.fix:
Smooth the offset instead of the position:
- Keep chaseOff (a Vector3).
- Target offset = −26·v̂ + 5.5·upBody, where upBody is (0,1,0).applyQuaternion(s.q) blended 30 % toward world up.
- chaseOff.lerp(target, 1−exp(−4dt)); camera = s.pos + chaseOff.
- Set camera.up to a smoothed blend of world up and body up before lookAt, then restore it as the cockpit branch does at f16Fly.js:268-271.
- Keep the ground clamp.

Optionally add 'flyby' as a fifth camera: placed 400 m ahead and 30 m to the side of the flight path, held fixed until the jet is 600 m past. It is the natural camera to showcase the Doppler.

findings.title: Minor model inconsistencies
findings.evidence:
- f16Assist.js:192 computes kcas from atmosphere(s.pos.y). f16Fly.js:497 and f16Fly.js:138 use s.alt, the geodesic altitude. SEA_LEVEL is −0.9 m (core/f16Ground.js:16), so the two agree near the site but drift apart with the curvature drop: about 0.8 km at 100 km out and about 7 km at 300 km. Beyond ~100 km the assist's speed protections then work from too high an airspeed.
- FCS.departure { alpha: 29, rudderGain: 0.75 } (f16Aero.js:121) is never read.
- The 20° flaperon droop with the gear down (f16Flight.js:310) is visual only, with no lift or drag term. Lift-off and landing speeds still come out plausible (155-176 kt and 136-145 kt).
- Above about 15 km at Mach 1.4-1.6 with full AB, the extrapolated thrust (f16Flight.js:96-101) still allows an 8° climb to 72,000 ft. This belongs to the open H17 item in TRASPASO.
findings.fix: Use s.alt in the assist. Delete FCS.departure or wire it with a comment. Document the flaperon simplification in the f16Flight.js header list of approximations. Leave the supersonic thrust for H17.

plan:
Everything below follows the repo rules in CLAUDE.md:
- English UI text, Spanish README updated.
- `npm run check:static` before each commit; the full check at the end of the block.
- Synthesis constants live in src/data/f16.js tagged ESTIMATE. Nothing presented as measured.
- No new materials, which would count against the 290 budget.

A. F-16 SOUND (new file src/sim/f16Sound.js, about 330 lines; same shape as gt3Sound.js:129-225)

A1. Pure parameter layer, no WebAudio, exported for the node tests:
- `export const ENGINE_SOUND`, re-exported from data/f16.js, tag 'ESTIMATE':
  - n2Idle 0.70, n1Idle 0.45;
  - fanBpfMax ≈ 4500 Hz, hpcMax ≈ 9000 Hz, shaftMax ≈ 173 Hz (N1 at 100 %, ≈);
  - vjIdle 300, vjMil 700, vjMax 1050 m/s;
  - Dj = sqrt(4·LINES.nozzle.exitArea/π) ≈ 0.71 m (DERIVED);
  - St 0.2.
  - Every ≈ number gets a comment: chosen by ear, not a spectrum.
- `export function engineParams(s, prev = {})` returns { n1, n2, ab, load, fanHz, hpcHz, shaftHz, jetHz, roar, buzz, flame, light, out, stage }:
  - load = clamp(s.power/50, 0, 1); ab = clamp((s.power−50)/50, 0, 1).
  - n2 = flameout ? min(0.3, s.tas/600) : n2Idle + (1−n2Idle)·load. n1 is the same with n1Idle. The spool lag already lives in s.power (f16Flight.js:290-295), so do not add a second one.
  - jetHz = St·Vj/Dj, with Vj blended from idle through MIL to max.
  - buzz = sstep(0.85, 1, n1): the fan's buzz-saw tones.
  - light = prev.ab ≤ 0.02 && ab > 0.02; out = prev.ab > 0.02 && ab ≤ 0.02.
  - stage = floor(ab·5): F100 five-zone afterburner (≈).
  - flame = !flameout && !crashed.
- `export function propagation(src, srcVel, lis, lisVel, fwd, c)` returns { d, delay, doppler, inCone, theta, gain, cutoff, fanDir, jetDir }:
  - delay = d/c.
  - doppler = (c + vLis·r̂)/(c − vSrc·r̂), with r̂ pointing from source to listener.
  - inCone: if M_src ≤ 1, true. Otherwise true iff the angle between (lis−src) and −v̂ is less than μ = asin(1/M). The cone opens backwards.
  - gain = min(1, 30/d)·(inCone ? 1 : 0).
  - cutoff = clamp(20000·150/d, 600, 20000) for air absorption.
  - theta = angle between nose and listener.
  - fanDir = 0.35 + 0.65·max(0, cosθ)^1.5.
  - jetDir = 0.3 + 0.7·exp(−((θ−140°)/35°)²).

A2. Worklet `f16-f100`, string WORKLET as in gt3Sound.js:24-125, two output channels: ch0 front/inlet, ch1 rear/jet.
- Port message fields: { n1, n2, load, ab, fanHz, hpcHz, shaftHz, jetHz, buzz, on, light, out, stage, boom, cabin }. Smooth them per block as gt3 does (×0.25-0.3).
- ch0:
  - fan BPF tones at k = 1..3, amplitudes 1 / 0.4 / 0.15, times 0.5 + 0.5·n1;
  - buzz-saw: shaft orders 8-30 with fixed random phases and 1/k amplitudes, times buzz·0.6;
  - HPC whine at hpcHz, amplitude 0.05, louder at idle: ×(1.2 − load);
  - inlet howl: noise through two biquads tracking 600 + 900·n1 and 1500 + 1200·n1 Hz, Q 5, gain ∝ n1².
- ch1:
  - combustion and jet roar: three-stage one-pole pink noise, band-passed by a biquad at jetHz with Q 0.7, gain 0.15 + 0.85·load^1.2;
  - AB rumble: 20-80 Hz noise with 0.3-3 Hz random amplitude modulation, gain ∝ ab;
  - crackle: N-shaped impulses as in sim/sound.js, rate 30 + 270·ab per s, heavy-tailed amplitude (−log(rnd))², gain ∝ ab·(Vj/700)²;
  - light-off thump: an impulse rung through R(45 Hz, Q 2) plus a noise burst decaying in 0.25 s, gain 1.0; stage steps 0.35; 'out' gives a 0.5 whump;
  - boom: a double N-wave of 2 × 0.09 s, ±1, 0.1 s apart, on message boom:1.
- Both channels: soft clip with tanh and a DC block, as at gt3Sound.js:117-119.
- Fallback without the worklet: three oscillators (fan saw, HPC sine, jet noise source), as at gt3Sound.js:154-158.

A3. Graph, built in build() with the same AudioContext, comp and master setup as gt3Sound.js:132-167:
- External path: engine → ChannelSplitter → fanG / jetG (directivity) → extMix → extLp (cutoff) → extDelay (ctx.createDelay(30)) → extPanner (HRTF, rolloffFactor 0; listener orientation from the camera, as sim/sound.js:126) → extG → master.
- Cockpit path: engine (both channels summed) → cockLp (lowpass 700 Hz) plus cockPeak (peaking 120 Hz +6 dB) → cockG → master.
- Noise sources, each a looped noise buffer through a filter into a gain (as in gt3/h2r):
  - wind: bandpass at 300 + 6·tas, gain min(0.5, (qbar/40e3)^0.6). Cockpit ×1.0, chase ×0.7, tower/orbit 0 (no self-wind for a still listener); the airframe's own rush goes through the external chain as 0.3·that level.
  - ECS hiss (cockpit only): constant 0.04, highpass 3 kHz.
  - roll rumble: lowpass 180 Hz, gain ∝ min(1, tas/60) while wow; ×1.6 off pavement (ground().hard false).
  - brake squeal: bandpass 2200 Hz, Q 18, gain 0.2 when wow && brake && 0.5 < tas < 25 m/s.
  - gear and speed-brake buffet: lowpass 250 Hz, gain ∝ (gear·0.6 + sb)·min(1, qbar/20e3).
- One-shots, via a play(buffer, gain) helper like sim/sound.js:177:
  - touchdown chirp: band noise 1.5-3 kHz, 0.15 s, gain ∝ sink, plus a 60 Hz thud;
  - gear clunk when s.gear reaches 0 or 1 in flight;
  - crash explosion: lowpass 300 Hz noise, 1.5 s decay, plus crackle.

A4. API, the same as gt3: { enabled, contextState, ready (=!!N?.engine), level (current master target), setEnabled(on), update(s, pilot, view), crash(speed), stop() }.
- view = { camera, listener: Vector3, listenerVel, quaternion (camera), nozzle: Vector3 (world), dt, hard }.
- update():
  - engineParams → postMessage.
  - propagation → set the gains and filters with setTargetAtTime (tc 0.04).
  - extDelay.delayTime.linearRampToValueAtTime(delay, now + dt), but jump with setValueAtTime when |Δdelay| > 0.3 s (camera switch or restart).
  - Clamp the delay's rate of decrease to −0.95 per second so the Doppler stays finite.
  - Crossfade: cockpit → cockG 1, extG 0; otherwise the reverse.
  - Chase listener: pass listenerVel = s.vel, so the Doppler ≈ 1 automatically.
  - Touchdown edge: s.wow false→true with sink > 0.3 m/s.
  - Boom edge: inCone false→true while srcMach > 1, sending boom:1 once per crossing.
- Same visibilitychange suspend/resume block as gt3Sound.js:174-180.

A5. f16Fly.js wiring:
- import { createF16Sound } from './f16Sound.js'; `const sound = createF16Sound();` after f16Fly.js:98.
- Add 'KeyM' to CODES (f16Fly.js:105-106) and `case 'KeyM': setSound(!sound.enabled); break;` in the switch at f16Fly.js:121-129.
- `function setSound(on) { sound.setEnabled(on); note(sound.enabled ? 'Sound on: the F100, the afterburner, the wind and the wheels (synthesised)' : 'Sound off'); }`
- Gamepad: padEdge(g, 8, () => setSound(!sound.enabled)) in readPad (f16Fly.js:197-200).
- In apply() after placeCamera (f16Fly.js:486):
  - if (state.paused) sound.stop();
  - else sound.update(s, pilot, { camera: state.camera, listener: camera.position, listenerVel: (camera.position − lastCam)/dt, quaternion: camera.quaternion, nozzle: flame.getWorldPosition(tmp), dt, hard: onPavement(s.pos.x, s.pos.z) }).
- In judge(), where the crash is detected (f16Fly.js:382-384): sound.crash(s.crashed.speed).
- In reset() (f16Fly.js:448-470): sound.stop().
- In publish() readout (f16Fly.js:511): add `sound: sound.enabled`.
- Return object (f16Fly.js:522): add `sound, setSound`.

A6. f16Hud.js:
- After #f16-assist (line 30): `<button type="button" class="f16-btn" id="f16-sound" aria-pressed="false" title="Sound (M): the F100 turbofan, the afterburner, the wind and the wheels, synthesised; off until you turn it on">Sound <kbd>M</kbd></button>`.
- Add onSound to the createF16Hud params (line 17), and `$('#f16-sound').addEventListener('click', () => onSound?.())` next to lines 46-50.
- In update(): `$('#f16-sound').setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(!!r.sound))`.
- Append ' · <kbd>M</kbd> sound' to both .f16-keys lines (34-35).

A7. main.js:672: add `onSound: () => f16fly.setSound(!f16fly.sound.enabled),`.

A8. hud.js guide F-16 card (179-185): add `<dt><kbd>C</kbd> · <kbd>M</kbd></dt><dd>camera · sound (off until you turn it on)</dd>`, and drop C from the G·C·Esc row.

A9. README (Spanish): a section «El F-16 suena». Cover what is synthesised, the ≈ constants, the Doppler and the boom, cockpit vs external, and M / Sound.

B. HANDLING FIXES
- B1. Ground: f16Flight.js:371 lateral-acceleration steering limit, and f16Flight.js:389 slip-angle tyre with friction circle (finding 2). f16Assist.js:180-181: yaw-rate steering plus runway heading and centreline hold.
- B2. Assist: speed-hold autothrottle (st.vHold), auto level-off at 4-5,000 ft AGL, release of the low-speed protection, gearAuto fix, s.alt in kcas (finding 3). Publish readout.vHold.
- B3. Gear-down protection: a 135 KCAS floor and earlier GCAS (finding 4).
- B4. HUD:
  - export runwayCue(r) and draw the RWY bearing, distance and glide-slope dot;
  - draw 'A/T nnn' in simple mode;
  - clip the cockpit ladder to the combiner box and skip rungs over the bar;
  - add a 'SOUND' item to cfg when on: optional.
- B5. Camera: offset-smoothed chase with body-blended up (f16Fly.js:285-297); optional 'flyby' camera added to CAMERAS (f16Fly.js:29) and to the #f16-cam title.
- B6. Cleanups: FCS.departure; document the flaperon simplification.

C. TESTS
C1. tools/f16-check.mjs (headless). Import engineParams, propagation and the WORKLET string from f16Sound.js; the file must not touch window at import time.
1. 'sonido: el F100 sube de vueltas con el motor'. Sweep power 0/25/50/75/100: fanHz and n2 rise monotonically; n2(0) = 0.70; ab = 0 at power ≤ 50.
2. 'sonido: el carrete'. With throttle snapped idle→MIL on the reset airplane, fanHz is below 90 % of its MIL value at 2 s and above it by 6 s, because it follows s.power.
3. 'sonido: la postcombustión se enciende una vez'. Sweep the throttle 0.7→1.0→0.7: exactly one `light` event and one `out` event.
4. 'sonido: Doppler'. Listener at (0,0,300), source at 200 m/s along x from −2000 to +2000: doppler matches c/(c − v·cosφ) within 0.5 %, is above 1 before closest approach and below 1 after.
5. 'sonido: cono de Mach'. Same pass at M1.3: inCone is false while approaching and flips true exactly once; the boom edge fires once.
6. 'sonido: cabina'. Wind gain is monotonic in qbar and ≤ 0.5.
7. 'sonido: el worklet suena'. Evaluate WORKLET with stub `class AudioWorkletProcessor { constructor(){ this.port = {}; } }`, a registerProcessor that captures the class, and globalThis.sampleRate = 48000. Run process() for 200 blocks at idle, MIL, AB and AB with light:1: every sample finite and |y| ≤ 1; RMS idle < MIL < AB on ch1.
